provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Nigerian musical instruments
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to name Nigerian musical instruments.
The pupils should be able to sort instruments into groups.

Introduction:
We have heard music at festivals and in churches.
Today we will learn about instruments we see in Nigeria.

Content:
Nigerian instruments include drum, flute and shekere.
The drum makes loud sounds for celebrations.
The flute makes soft sounds like bird songs.
The shekere is made from gourds with beads.
We can sort them by how they make sound.

Class activity:
Let us make a shekere with a small gourd and beads.

Evaluation questions:
Name three Nigerian musical instruments.
Which instrument is made from a gourd?
How can we sort these instruments?

Summary:
We can name and sort Nigerian musical instruments.

topics.title: Instrument families
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify shakers and drums.
The pupils should be able to make simple sounds with instruments.

Introduction:
Last week we learned about Nigerian instruments.
Today we will learn about families of instruments.

Content:
Shakers are instruments that you shake.
Drums are instruments that you hit.
Shakers make sound by moving inside.
Drums make sound when you hit the top.
A shekere is a type of shaker.
A talking drum is a type of drum.

Class activity:
Let us make sounds with our bodies and with simple instruments.

Evaluation questions:
What is a shaker instrument?
What is a drum instrument?
How do we make sounds with shakers?

Summary:
Shakers and drums are two families of instruments.

topics.title: Drawing: festivals
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to draw a festival scene.
The pupils should be able to colour with meaning.

Introduction:
We have seen festivals like Christmas and New Year.
Today we will draw what we see at festivals.

Content:
A festival scene has people, food and decorations.
We can draw people dancing and eating.
We can draw colourful decorations.
Colours have meaning in drawings.
Red means happiness and green means life.
We use bright colours for festivals.

Class activity:
Let us draw a scene of the New Year festival.

Evaluation questions:
What do we see at a festival?
What does red colour mean in drawings?
How do we show happiness in our drawing?

Summary:
We can draw festival scenes with meaningful colours.

topics.title: Weaving with paper and raffia
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain the over and under method.
The pupils should be able to make a small mat.

Introduction:
We have seen mats in our homes.
Today we will learn how to weave with paper and raffia.

Content:
Weaving means to go over and under threads.
Paper strips can be used for weaving.
Raffia comes from palm trees.
We start with the warp threads vertical.
Then we weave the weft threads over and under.
This makes a pattern on our mat.

Class activity:
Let us weave a small mat using coloured paper strips.

Evaluation questions:
What does weaving mean?
What is the over and under method?
What can we use for weaving?

Summary:
We can make small mats using the over and under weaving method.

topics.title: Cultural dances
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify Bata and Atilogwu dances.
The pupils should be able to learn simple dance steps.

Introduction:
We have seen people dance at weddings and festivals.
Today we will learn about Nigerian cultural dances.

Content:
The Bata dance comes from the Yoruba people.
The Atilogwu dance comes from the Igbo people.
Bata dance has drum beats that talk.
Atilogwu dance has quick steps and jumps.
We can learn simple steps from these dances.
Dancing tells stories and shows happiness.

Class activity:
Let us learn simple steps from the Bata and Atilogwu dances.

Evaluation questions:
Where does Bata dance come from?
What does Atilogwu dance look like?
Why do people dance at festivals?

Summary:
We can learn simple steps from Nigerian cultural dances.

topics.title: Mask and masquerade talk
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify masks in festivals.
The pupils should be able to make a paper mask.

Introduction:
We have seen masquerades during festivals like Durbar.
Today we will learn about masks and masquerades.

Content:
Masks cover the face of the masquerade.
Masks can be made of wood, cloth or paper.
Masks show spirits or animals.
They are used in festivals and ceremonies.
Different masks have different meanings.
Some masks scare away bad spirits.

Class activity:
Let us make paper masks for our classroom festival.

Evaluation questions:
What are masks used for?
What are masks made of?
What do some masks scare away?

Summary:
We can make paper masks and know their uses in festivals.

topics.title: Bead work
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to string beads in a pattern.
The pupils should be able to make simple bead work.

Introduction:
We have seen beads on necklaces and bracelets.
Today we will learn how to make bead work.

Content:
Beads come in many colours and sizes.
We string beads on thread or wire.
We can make patterns with colours.
Red, white and green are Nigerian colours.
Bead work can be for necklaces and bracelets.
Some bead work tells stories.

Class activity:
Let us string beads to make a simple bracelet.

Evaluation questions:
What do we use to string beads?
What patterns can we make with beads?
What can we make with beads?

Summary:
We can make simple bead work by stringing beads in patterns.

topics.title: Drama: folk stories
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to act out the hare story.
The pupils should be able to make simple costumes.

Introduction:
We have heard folk stories like the tortoise and the birds.
Today we will act out a story with simple costumes.

Content:
The hare is a clever character in folk stories.
We can use paper to make animal ears and tails.
Simple costumes help us become characters.
We can use our voices to show feelings.
Acting out stories helps us learn lessons.

Class activity:
Let us act out the hare and the tortoise race with simple costumes.

Evaluation questions:
Who is the hare in folk stories?
What do we use for simple costumes?
What do we learn from acting out stories?

Summary:
We can act out folk stories with simple costumes and learn lessons.

topics.title: Making greeting cards
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to make a card for a friend.
The pupils should be able to write neat lettering.

Introduction:
We have received birthday cards from friends.
Today we will learn how to make greeting cards.

Content:
A greeting card has a fold in the middle.
We can draw pictures on the front.
We write messages inside for our friends.
We use bright colours for the card.
Neat lettering makes the card nice.
We can use stickers to decorate the card.

Class activity:
Let us make a birthday card for our friend with neat lettering.

Evaluation questions:
What do we put on the front of a card?
What do we write inside a card?
How do we make our lettering neat?

Summary:
We can make nice greeting cards with neat lettering for our friends.

topics.title: Revision and assessment
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recall term work.
The pupils should be able to display their work.

Introduction:
We have learned many things this term.
Today we will revise and show our best work.

Content:
We learned about Nigerian musical instruments.
We learned about cultural dances and masks.
We learned to draw, weave and make cards.
We also learned about bead work and drama.
We can show our best work in the classroom.
We can tell others what we made and why.

Class activity:
Let us display our best work and explain what we did.

Evaluation questions:
What is your favourite thing you learned this term?
How do you make a simple mat?
What can you tell about cultural dances?

Summary:
We can recall what we learned and display our best work.
